_note: Framework crosswalk — structure only. The 11 pillars in pillars.json remain the
canonical capability model; frameworks map INTO them and never the other way.
PROJECTION RULE — LEAF LEVEL ONLY. A dimension with children carries no crosswalk
entries and is never projected directly. Its score rolls up from its children,
inside the framework, never across the pillar side. COBIT's APO14 and its ten
sub-practices must never both count a pillar: that double-counts the same evidence
and inflates the component it appears in. The same holds for the three DGI groups.
WEIGHT is the dimension's share WITHIN ITS PARENT (within the framework for level 1).
Effective leaf weight is the product down the chain, so leaf weights over a whole
framework sum to 1.0 and the induced pillar weight vector also sums to 1.0. That is
what makes the four scorecards reconcile against one another.
WEIGHTS ARE DGIW'S EDITORIAL JUDGEMENT, NOT PUBLISHED CONTENT. None of these four
frameworks publishes relative weights for its own dimensions. The dimension NAMES
and CODES are published structure and are marked with a per-framework confidence;
the numbers beside them are ours and are the first thing a reviewer should argue
with. structureConfidence and structureNotes record where that line falls.
SCALES DIFFER AND ARE NOT YET RECONCILED. DCAM scores 1-6, COBIT 0-5, DGIW 1-5.
scaleMin/scaleMax are recorded here so C2 can rescale explicitly. Nothing in C1
reads them.
Sorted by id, code-unit order. Ids are allocation-ordered and never renumbered.

frameworks.name: DAMA-DMBOK2 Data Management Body of Knowledge
frameworks.structureNotes: The eleven knowledge areas of the DMBOK2 wheel, with Data Governance at the hub. Well-established and widely reproduced; I am confident in the list and the naming. DMBOK2 itself publishes no maturity scale — the 1-5 here is DGIW's own scale, not DAMA's. The book's supporting chapters (Data Handling Ethics, Big Data & Data Science, Data Management Maturity Assessment, Organization & Role Expectations) are deliberately NOT modelled as knowledge areas, because they are not on the wheel.

frameworks.name: Data Management Capability Assessment Model
frameworks.structureNotes: FLAGGED FOR REVIEW. The eight components below are DCAM v2.2 as I recall it, and the exact published wording of several component names is uncertain — 'Data Management Program & Funding' and 'Data Control Environment' in particular may differ in the source. DCAM v3.0 reorganised the model and this is NOT v3.0; versionLabel says v2.2 deliberately rather than claiming currency. DCAM's capability and sub-capability levels beneath each component are NOT authored here: I do not recall them reliably enough to put in front of an auditor, and an absent level is recoverable where a fabricated one is not. The 1-6 scale is DCAM's six-point scoring (Not Initiated / Conceptual / Developmental / Defined / Achieved / Enhanced) and I am reasonably confident in it.

frameworks.name: DGI Data Governance Framework
frameworks.structureNotes: The ten components are well documented and I am confident in them. The three groupings used here as parents — Rules & Rules of Engagement, People & Organizational Bodies, Processes — are how the published DGI diagram arranges those ten; I am treating a presentational grouping as a formal level, which is a modelling choice rather than published hierarchy. Flagged because a reviewer may reasonably want the ten flat. DGI publishes no maturity scale; 1-5 is DGIW's.

frameworks.name: COBIT 2019 — governance objectives and Managed Data
frameworks.structureNotes: The five EDM governance objectives are high confidence, including EDM05 'Ensured Stakeholder Engagement' (renamed from COBIT 5's 'Ensure Stakeholder Transparency'). APO14 Managed Data was new in COBIT 2019 and carries ten management practices APO14.01-APO14.10. The titles below were originally paraphrased from memory; they have since been checked against a public COBIT 2019 reference and two were corrected (APO14.03 lost a stray 'the', APO14.08 now reads 'life cycle' as two words). They have NOT been checked against the ISACA publication itself, which is the only source an audit function should accept — that verification is still outstanding and is why structureConfidence stays at medium rather than rising. COBIT 2019 capability levels run 0-5, which is why scaleMin is 0 and not 1. Giving APO14 55% of the framework weight is DGIW's judgement: it is the only data-specific objective in COBIT, so a COBIT-framed DATA assessment cannot sensibly be dominated by the generic governance domain.
